one_month_reasoning: One stock-specific event falls in the window: Q3 2026 results after the close on 2026-10-20 [19][30]. Consensus is about $2.91B revenue and $2.64 non-GAAP EPS [19]. The supervisor was right that my 7-for-7 positive Q3 report-day record was a small sample. I re-ran it on every quarterly report since 2019 in my own daily data [27]: 14 of 31 report days were positive, the median was -1.5%, the mean +0.3%, the average absolute move 5.9% and the standard deviation 7.1%. That is effectively a coin flip with fat tails, and 2026 has already produced -14.1% (July) and +7.2% (April). The comp is tough: Q3 2025 da Vinci procedures grew ~19% [40], and Q3 2025 EPS of $2.40 included a $0.12 tax benefit [40]. This is also the call where management sizes EUP 2.0 [43], which is a headline risk. The one analog I found, the Q3 2020 print right after EUP 1.0 launched on 2020-10-01 [42], saw the stock rise 1.6% on the day [27], so I do not treat the quantification as clearly negative. The stock also rallied ~15% in September to $406.63 on Sep 30 and gave back 1.3% on Oct 1 [27]. Macro: the FOMC meets Oct 27-28, with Kalshi/Polymarket at about 65-67% hold and 33-35% hike on Sep 30 [21][41]. The 10-year is 5.29% (FRED, 2026-09-30) and rising [39]. A Section 232 device proclamation is possible but unscheduled [16]. I drop the upward tilt: median ~$400.5 (flat to slightly below today), with 11.8% one-month volatility from t(5) tails. My own data gives 12.2% for 21-day windows that contain a report since 2019, against 9.6% for all windows [27].

fair_value.method: Blend of four methods, each net of a ~$5/share litigation haircut: forward P/E (NTM non-GAAP EPS $12.9 at Oct-2027 x 31.5x = $406, less $5 = $401, weight 0.45); EV/EBITDA (NTM EBITDA $6.39B x 20.5x + $10.3B net cash over 355M shares = $398, less $5 = $393, weight 0.30); trailing GAAP P/E (trailing GAAP EPS at Oct-2027 $9.59 x 42x = $403, less $5 = $398, weight 0.20); and a shrunk own-history drift (+8% = $433, weight 0.05). The blend is about $400.

$12.09 x 1.13. Bloomberg consensus EBITDA grows 14.1% from FY2027 to FY2028 [25]; I take slightly less for EPS.

Management calls EUP 2.0 'directionally similar to 2020' and will size it on the Q3 call [43]; EUP 1.0 cut per-use instrument cost by 9-15% for customers [42]. The supervisor's plausible range is a 1-3% I&A-per-procedure drag in 2027. I&A is roughly 60% of revenue [1], so a ~2% drag is ~1.2% of revenue, or ~1.5% of EPS at high incremental margin.

HCA's 10-Q shows uninsured admissions +23.4%, exchange admissions -15% and outpatient surgeries -3.4% [44], a larger headwind than I sized in round 1 (HCA surgeries down 2-3% [35]). Medicaid work requirements start 2027-01-01.

Today is ~34x NTM ($401.24 / $11.76) [2]. The Fed hiked on 2026-09-16 [46]. The 10-year is at 5.29% on 2026-09-30, up from 5.01% on the day of the hike [39]. Medtech has de-rated to a median ~16x NTM against a 25x five-year median [26], with peers at 14-22x [25]. EPS growth slows to low teens. Following the supervisor's advice to put macro into the multiple rather than the drift, I take 31.5x instead of 33x.

On 2026-08-13 the Ninth Circuit reversed the SIS judgment [45], which strengthens the hospital class whose trial starts 2027-09-14. The supervisor and agent_3 put the expected value at ~$5/share; I accept it as a left-tail item.

bear.story: The Q3 call sizes EUP 2.0 at the top of the 1-3% range [43]. In January, 2027 procedure growth is guided to ~10-12% as ACA attrition and Medicaid work requirements bite [44] and GLP-1s weigh on bariatrics [38]. Ottava and Hugo general-surgery wins add price pressure [32][34], and a Section 232 device tariff may land [16]. The 10-year moves past 5.5% [39]. The hospital class trial (2027-09-14) goes badly after the Ninth Circuit reversal [45]. NTM EPS falls to ~$12.2 and the multiple to ~24x, toward peers [25][26]. This resembles 2013 [10][11].

base.story: Procedure growth runs ~13%, and EUP 2.0 costs ~1.5% of EPS and slowly stimulates volume, as EUP 1.0 was meant to [42]. dV5 trade-ins stay strong [1], Ottava stays capacity-limited [32] and the litigation drags on. NTM EPS ~$12.9 at ~31.5-32x, roughly flat to +2%.

bull.story: EUP 2.0 lands at the low end and lifts volume, competitive fears fade [32][4], elective volumes stabilise as the ACA shock laps, and long rates roll over from 5.3% [39]. The stock re-rates to ~41x NTM EPS of $13.4, repeating its 2022-23 recovery [28] toward the upper analyst targets [2][3].

thesis_break_reason: $300 is ~9% below the July 2026 low of $328.57 and ~23x my NTM non-GAAP EPS of $12.9 (~31x trailing GAAP), below the 10-year GAAP trailing P/E floor of 33.5x [6]. A trade there would most likely mean estimates are being cut, not just the multiple: 2027 procedure growth guided below ~11%, an EUP 2.0 drag well above ~3% of I&A per procedure [43], visible share loss to Ottava or Hugo, a device tariff, or an adverse turn in the hospital class case after the Ninth Circuit reversal [45]. The worst 12-month outcome after a comparable drawdown since 2010 was -18% [28], about $330, so $300 is outside ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact-checks changed four things. (1) The ACA headwind is larger than I had it: HCA's 10-Q shows uninsured admissions +23.4%, exchange -15% and outpatient surgeries -3.4% [44]. (2) EUP 2.0 will be sized on the Q3 call, plausibly a 1-3% I&A-per-procedure drag in 2027 [43]; EUP 1.0 cut customers' per-use cost 9-15% [42]. (3) The Ninth Circuit reversed SIS on 2026-08-13, which strengthens the hospital class whose trial starts 2027-09-14 [45]; I take a ~$5/share haircut. (4) My base rates were overweighted. I re-ran report-day reactions on all 31 quarters since 2019: 14 positive, median -1.5% [27]. So the 7-for-7 Q3 record was noise and I drop the 1-month up-tilt. I cut the drift method to weight 0.05 at +8%. Where I disagree with the supervisor: it could not confirm my 5.29% 10-year yield and used ~5.0% from 2026-09-16, but FRED shows 5.01% on Sep 16 rising to 5.29% on Sep 30 [39]. The higher figure stands and is dated, and I put it into the multiples as advised: forward P/E 33x to 31.5x, EV/EBITDA 21x to 20.5x. I also fixed a trailing-EPS timing error in my GAAP method. With NTM EPS of $12.9 (consensus-based $13.27, less 1.5% for EUP and 1% for coverage), the methods give $401, $393, $398 and $433, which blend to $400, down from $425. That is below the supervisor's ~$420. The gap is mainly because I blend FY27 and FY28 for NTM EPS at Oct-2027 and haircut for both EUP and the larger ACA headwind, while the supervisor appears to apply 31.5x to full 2028E EPS. Scenarios are $295/$410/$555 at 25/50/25% (mean ~$418, skewed right). The ladder uses a t(5) log distribution with median $405 (fair value plus about half a market-like drift) and 34% vol (long-run 31-33% weekly, 37% 1-year realized [27][28]). I shaded P(>=281/321) down by ~0.5 point for the litigation tail. That gives P(>=401) = 0.51 (from 0.57), P(>=321) = 0.785 and P(>=602) = 0.10. Analyst targets ($476 average [2]) remain sentiment evidence above my median. Research limits: I used 7 follow-up searches and fetches. The HCA 10-Q, Wells Fargo recap, Ninth Circuit opinion and CNBC Fed piece come from the supervisor's evidence and were not re-read by me.
